COULD_NOT_SETTLE: The capability inventory proposed settling the 8-anionic-initialization AUC cost by comparing anionic and neutral init lineages in a completed campaign. That is NOT possible from the stored artifacts: the archive's 32 root entries are already-edited bootstrap products, not the init molecules, and no provenance pointer crosses that boundary. Lineage back to a specific init molecule is unrecoverable, so the anionic question needs a fresh instrumented run, not a re-read.
FINDING: The chemistry collapse happens in TWO separable stages with DIFFERENT causes, and the first one is task-independent.
STAGE_1_bootstrap: init -> gen 0 loses QED>=0.6 from 87.5% to 46.9% -- roughly FORTY POINTS -- in a single edit, BEFORE any scored search can have informed anything, and identically for every task. Heavy atoms RISE here (20 -> 22), so this is not shrinkage. This is the missing chemical prior in its purest form: one random legal edit from a drug-like molecule destroys drug-likeness about 40% of the time.
STAGE_2_search: gen 0 -> gen >=1 takes QED>=0.6 from 46.9% to 16-22% while heavy atoms FALL 22 -> 11-16. The size collapse appears only here, which matches the parent allocator handing ~80% of parent mass to at most 8 molecules whose niche centres replay as 1-3 atom fragments, score-independently.
WHY_THE_SEPARATION_MATTERS: The two defects are now attributable to different layers and can be fixed and measured independently: stage 1 is proposal quality (no learned prior over real chemistry anywhere in the PMO path), stage 2 is parent allocation. Neither fix alone should be expected to recover the full gap, and a repair that only moves one stage should not be read as solving the collapse.
